name: Bombay Frankie
steps: Mix the flour with 3 g salt, 10 ml oil and 135 ml water. Knead for 5 minutes to a soft dough, adding the remaining 20 ml water only if needed. Cover and rest 15 minutes. Boil the potatoes until a knife slips through, drain completely, peel and crush coarsely. Cut paneer into small cubes and slice the onion thinly.

For the green chutney, blend 25 g coriander, all the mint, green chilli, ginger, 20 ml lemon juice, 1 g salt and the remaining measured 30 ml water. Keep the chutney thick so it does not soak the rotis.

Heat 20 ml oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Brown the paneer cubes lightly for 2 minutes and lift them out. Add the crushed potato, ground cumin, Kashmiri chilli and 4 g salt; stir and cook for 4–5 minutes until hot and fairly dry. Fold the paneer back in with 10 g chopped coriander and 3 g chaat masala. Divide the filling into four equal portions.

Divide the rested dough into four balls and roll each into a thin 20–22 cm round. Cook on a hot dry tawa for about 1 minute on each side until spotted and cooked through. Brush each warm roti with a little of the remaining 15 ml oil and keep covered so it stays flexible.

Spread one quarter of the green chutney on each roti. Put one filling portion down the middle and scatter the sliced onion over it. Sprinkle the remaining 3 g chaat masala, 1 g salt and 15 ml lemon juice evenly across all four rolls. Fold the bottom edge over the filling, roll tightly and wrap the lower half in food-safe paper. Serve hot, one frankie per person.
tips: The photograph shows the paneer-and-potato version of this Mumbai-style roll. For a milder family meal, remove the chilli seeds before blending. Check that packaged chaat masala is vegetarian and contains no ingredients your household avoids.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
